decisions.feedback: The user authorizes resolving OQ-1 with the recommended server-held state: one shared in-memory game, page refresh retrieves/resumes the current board, concurrent state changes are serialized, and reset returns an empty board with X to move. Record this as a resolved choice in the assumptions/open-questions section and preserve the existing acceptance criteria, terminal behavior, and bounded local scope. This is a requested clarification, not an implementation failure; do not introduce new features or requirements.

The plan needs two corrections before build. (1) Honor the resolved server-held state/refresh requirement: declare a read-only state retrieval endpoint (for example GET /state), or equivalent initial hydration, and explain that page load/refresh retrieves the existing board without resetting it. Include tests for retrieval after moves, refresh/second-tab hydration, and unchanged state on failed requests. Current static embedded HTML plus only move/reset endpoints does not establish that behavior. (2) Choose one concrete web startup interface and use it consistently throughout architecture, stories, and documentation: an explicit web mode with loopback default and an address override is sufficient; remove conflicting web-subcommand versus addr-only alternatives. Preserve the terminal default, existing acceptance criteria, no-third-party-dependencies constraint, protected ttt binary, and final build/test/vet/lint/story gates inside the build Agent. Do not add features or a separate lint stage.
